project.name: ota-name-generator
project.objective: Given one StayVista property URL, read the property page, rank what actually sells it, and recommend the OTA title to publish on Airbnb, Booking.com, MakeMyTrip, Agoda and Goibibo.

stack: headless Chrome/Edge over CDP (no dependency; uses the installed browser)

patterns: Every fact carries {value, source, evidence}; anything not on the fact sheet cannot appear in a name
LLM proposes, deterministic engine decides — AI names are re-validated and re-scored locally
Title candidates are prioritised segments, so shortening drops the least important part instead of truncating
USP `feature` de-duplicates alternative wordings of one thing; USP `category` limits one per title
Zero runtime dependencies; the Anthropic SDK is lazily imported and optional
Extraction is a chain of five routes whose results merge; the trace is part of the API response
Trusted zone (the listing about itself) vs page zone (everything else on the page): only the trusted zone can name a property
Proximity language invalidates setting/view claims but not amenity claims
A route that has proved pointless for a URL is not repeated in the session (known placeholders)
A page the user captured in their own browser is a first-class route, trusted for its property section only
The URL itself is the floor of the fact sheet, so an unreadable page still yields a partial analysis
StayVista is the source of truth; its unavailable-amenity list denies a feature outright
Negation counts only in the run-up to a match, never anywhere in the sentence
A phrase that upgrades what the page confirms is refused even when every word is allowed
Per-OTA titles come from platform profiles, and pass the same accuracy gate and scorer as every other name

worksEndToEnd: StayVista property URL -> full read in under a second -> ranked USPs -> five structured options -> recommendation
One title per OTA (Airbnb / Booking.com / MakeMyTrip / Agoda / Goibibo), each within that platform's ceiling and shown as a card with a glyph, counter and Copy button
Unavailable amenities honoured: The Infinity Heaven denies 9 features, none of which can enter a name
Airbnb URL -> direct read; Agoda URL -> browser rendering; MakeMyTrip/Goibibo -> placeholder detected, capture route offered
Browser capture, URL-facts floor, manual corrections, accuracy gate, optional Claude pass

decisions.decision: Deterministic engine is the product; Claude is an optional enhancement
decisions.rationale: No API key was set, and the accuracy rules are easier to guarantee in code. The tool works fully offline and the AI pass cannot introduce unverified claims.

decisions.decision: Zero runtime dependencies (node:http, hand-rolled HTML/JSON extraction)
decisions.rationale: Keeps install trivial on a RAM-constrained laptop and avoids a framework for a single-page internal tool.

decisions.decision: Every fact carries a source and an evidence quote; names may only use fact-sheet vocabulary
decisions.rationale: The brief's hardest requirement is never inventing information. A vocabulary gate makes that checkable rather than aspirational, and it also polices AI output.

decisions.decision: No attempt to defeat bot protection, CAPTCHAs or login walls; offer a paste path instead
decisions.rationale: Explicitly required by the brief and the right call for OTA terms of service. Pasting the page the user already has open gives the same analysis quality.

decisions.decision: Split USP identity into `feature` (de-duplicate wordings) and `category` (one per title)
decisions.rationale: A pool table and indoor games are different facts about a property but should not both sit in one title; 'Pool' and 'Private Pool' are the same fact and only the stronger wording should survive.

decisions.decision: Titles are prioritised segments, shortened by substitution then segment removal
decisions.rationale: Guarantees the character limit without truncating mid-word and without losing the strongest USP, and lets the UI report exactly what was shortened or dropped.

decisions.decision: A JSON response is a listing to parse, not an error
decisions.rationale: The reported MakeMyTrip failure was a content-type rejection. Responses are now classified and JSON payloads mined by key name; only binary is rejected. It also exposed that MMT/Goibibo send byte-sized OK placeholders, which is now named explicitly.

decisions.decision: Render with the installed browser over CDP, and stop at gates
decisions.rationale: Client-rendered OTAs (Agoda, Goibibo) can only be read by executing their own app. Uses installed Chrome/Edge with zero dependencies; reports blocked on any challenge, CAPTCHA or login wall rather than trying to pass it.

decisions.decision: Split every page into a trusted zone and a page zone
decisions.rationale: Rendering surfaced neighbouring listings, filter labels and area guides as if they were this property's features (a city hotel came out as River View Farm House). Only what the listing says about itself can name it; the rest is reported and confirmable.

decisions.decision: Capture the listing from the browser the user is already using
decisions.rationale: MakeMyTrip and Goibibo serve a placeholder to anything outside their own site session, rendering included. The page on the user's screen is the only readable copy, and a user-initiated capture of it is within their gift; automating the site navigation that removes the placeholder would not be.

decisions.decision: The URL is a fact source of last resort
decisions.rationale: The listing path carries the property name and city. Showing an error while holding those facts was wasteful; they now seed a partial analysis, labelled From the URL and outranked by anything read from the page.

decisions.decision: StayVista is the source of truth, and its unavailable-amenity list is a denial
decisions.rationale: StayVista publishes what a property does not have. Honouring that is stronger than any text heuristic: The Infinity Heaven denies 9 features, and a Pool/Jacuzzi search-category tag on another villa would otherwise have invented a jacuzzi. Text negation is also guarded, but only in the run-up to a match.

decisions.decision: One title per OTA, from platform conventions rather than one universal name
decisions.rationale: Airbnb shows the location and truncates; Booking.com treats the title as the property name; MMT/Goibibo guests search by BHK and city; Agoda's audience does not read BHK. Conventions, not quoted policy — stated as such in the module, and overridable.

assumptions: One property per analysis; bulk/Excel flows are explicitly out of scope
Default title limit 50 characters, adjustable per analysis in the UI
Indian villa/homestay vocabulary is the priority (BHK, bonfire, caretaker cum cook, jhula, sigri)
The user may legitimately paste listing content from a page they have open; that counts as a verified source
nextSteps: Sanity-check the per-OTA conventions against what your OTA account managers advise, and adjust the profiles in lib/otastyle.js if any platform differs
Run more StayVista properties and add USP wording the catalog misses (an in-house bar was one such gap)
Decide the house rule for NCR properties whose name and city field disagree (Faridabad vs New Delhi) — the tool surfaces both and the correction panel switches it
lessonsLearned: MakeMyTrip and Goibibo answer listing URLs from outside their own site session with a byte-sized OK placeholder (6 and 8 bytes) under a JSON content type — a rendering browser gets the same, so there is nothing to parse and nothing to retry
The fallback that works for those OTAs is the user's own browser: a bookmarklet or console snippet posting the page's visible content to the local server, which is user-initiated and bypasses nothing
A site's CSP can block the snippet's fetch, so the snippet falls back to opening a local receive page with the payload in the URL fragment (navigation is not restricted by connect-src)
Booking.com answers automated requests with an AWS WAF challenge; Agoda ships an empty shell that rendering can read; Airbnb serves the listing directly
Headless Chrome needs an explicit --user-agent: with the default HeadlessChrome UA, MakeMyTrip fails the request with ERR_HTTP2_PROTOCOL_ERROR
Node has a global WebSocket, so CDP needs no dependency; Chrome writes its port to <user-data-dir>/DevToolsActivePort with --remote-debugging-port=0

Any page read in bulk brings its neighbours: recommendation carousels, filter lists and area guides all look like evidence unless zoned out, and a neighbour's stronger wording can even displace the property's own feature in de-duplication
Airbnb keeps everything in the data-deferred-state-0 JSON blob while its rendered HTML text is only ~700 characters
Agoda's ld+json is present but empty and its initParams blob is config only — page-source pastes do not help there; visible page text does

Writing large JS through bash heredocs mangles regex-heavy content and fails outright on apostrophes; use the Write tool for new files, write patch scripts to a file, and use raw strings for anything containing \b (a non-raw string once wrote literal 0x08 bytes)
pkill does not reliably stop node on Windows; stop the server by matching its command line via PowerShell/CIM or the old process keeps the port and you test stale code
